scope: Proposition 2.1 (The two polynomial vacua) of the manuscript “Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks” (preprints/Radial-transfer-estimates-and-polygon-length-laws-for-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 02d2e8df0dcf370b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 12-13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each of the choices (p, η) = (1, −i), (2, i), there is a unique polynomial family VN , N ≥ 0, satisfying the degree, exchange, rotation, deletion, and pair requirements above. It lies in the link image, its empty coefficient Dp = V empty N is not identically zero, and Tη(z; u)VN (z) = VN (z) 12 as a rational identity for every auxiliary parameter u. The normalized rational vector VN /Dp extends regularly to homogeneous sites and there equals the empty-normalized stationary state obtained from either physical transfer limit.
